summary: Benoist–Wittenberg formulate the real integral Hodge conjecture in the equivariant cohomology of X(C) and, assuming it for 1-cycles, describe the algebraic classes on X(R), the existence of curves of even geometric genus and the image of torsion 1-cycles (Theorems A and C); for rationally connected or simply connected Calabi–Yau threefolds they reduce the conjecture to these conditions (Theorem B). Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item (the four Questions added), every missing item is routed exactly once, and ten findings are recorded. Theorem A(ii)/3.16(ii) is false for curves with a real point (E1), the Example 4.4 construction is impossible (E3), and Remarks 5.10 are announced without proof (E10). Not formalised.

items.name: Real closed field carrier
items.statement: A field R is real closed when it is semireal, exactly one of x and −x is a square for x≠0, and every odd-degree polynomial has a root; use the pinned IsRealClosed class rather than a new field carrier.
items.note: This item is only the field carrier, not the algebraic-closure theorem for R(i).

api.name: RealCycles.realClosed.characterise
api.statement: Recover the square/nonnegative equivalence after choosing the compatible ordering.

api.name: RealCycles.realClosed.compatibility
api.statement: Use the existing odd-degree root interface.

api.name: RealCycles.realClosed.functoriality
api.statement: Transport along field equivalences; do not infer an ordered topology comparison for arbitrary R.

items.name: Derived category of an abelian category
items.statement: For an abelian category A with a chosen localization universe, DerivedCategory A is the localization of Z-indexed cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, with localization functor Q.

api.name: RealCycles.derivedCategory.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.derivedCategory.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.derivedCategory.functoriality
api.statement: Use the existing localization universal property, not a new formal triangulated placeholder.

items.name: Sheaf cohomology carrier
items.statement: For an abelian sheaf F on a Grothendieck site with sheafification and Ext, H^n(F)=Ext^n(Z_const,F) for n≥0; at degree zero a terminal object identifies it with global sections.

items.name: Algebraic cycle carrier
items.statement: For a scheme X and a coefficient type with zero, AlgebraicCycle X R is the type of locally finitely supported coefficient functions on points of X, viewed as generic points of irreducible closed subsets.

api.name: RealCycles.cyclesCarrier.characterise
api.statement: Use local finiteness rather than an unjustified global finite sum for arbitrary schemes.

api.name: RealCycles.cyclesCarrier.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.cyclesCarrier.functoriality
api.statement: Reuse map_id; composition on Chow groups still requires proof.

items.name: Periodic finite cyclic group cohomology
items.statement: For a representation A of a finite cyclic group generated by g, H^0 is the invariant kernel; positive even cohomology is the homology of N→A→(g−1), and odd cohomology the homology of (g−1)→A→N, with N the cyclic norm.
items.note: Specialized integral C2 products and equivariant sheaves still need adapters.

items.name: Shapiro isomorphism for representations
items.statement: For a commutative ring k, subgroup S≤G and k-linear S-representation A, H^n(G,Coind_S^G A)≅H^n(S,A) for every n≥0.
items.note: This does not on its own prove the sheaf-equivariant geometric Shapiro comparison.

items.name: Pure Hodge structure carrier
items.statement: On a complex vector space with conjugation, a pure weight-n Hodge structure is an exhaustive decreasing filtration F with F^p complementary to conjugate F^(n+1−p); reuse HodgeStructureOn and its integral base-change specialization.
items.note: No geometric Hodge decomposition, integral Hodge conjecture or cycle class is inferred from this carrier.

api.name: RealCycles.hodgeCarrier.characterise
api.statement: Recover the conjugate filtration using conjF.

api.name: RealCycles.hodgeCarrier.compatibility
api.statement: Use the lattice complexification specialization HodgeStructure.

api.name: RealCycles.hodgeCarrier.functoriality
api.statement: Transport along a conjugation-compatible linear equivalence through the existing API.

items.name: Chow and intersection interfaces
items.statement: For smooth varieties over R, rational equivalence gives CH^k; proper pushforward, flat pullback, intersection products, Chern classes and projective-bundle/blowup formulas obey their degree and projection formulas.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Characteristic-zero resolution and factorization
items.statement: Smooth proper birational varieties in characteristic zero admit the blowup/blowdown factorizations in smooth centers used to compare codimension-two and 1-cycle class defects; resolve singular cycle supports before smooth purity.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Norm-residue theorem
items.statement: For a field F, integer n invertible in F and q≥0, the norm-residue map K_q^M(F)/n→H^q_et(F,μ_n^⊗q) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Smooth-pair étale purity
items.statement: For a smooth codimension-c closed pair over a perfect field with invertible torsion coefficients Λ, i^!Λ_X≅Λ_Z(−c)[−2c], compatibly with Gysin, products and cycle classes.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Geometric étale trace and duality
items.statement: For smooth pure-d-dimensional separated finite-type schemes over a field, the geometric finite-coefficient compact-support trace pairing and its proper specialization have complementary degree 2d and twist d, with derived integral versions retaining Ext terms.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Correspondence action
items.statement: Chow correspondences act on realizations by pullback, cup with the cycle class and proper pushforward, respecting composition and diagonal identity.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Complex threefold integral Hodge theorem
items.statement: For a smooth projective complex threefold that is uniruled, or has trivial canonical bundle and first Betti number zero, every integral Hodge class of degree four is algebraic.
items.note: Roadmap promise only, not a library implementation; exact supporting proof still requires the source audit indicated in gaps.

items.name: Semi-algebraic real and complex loci
items.statement: For X/R finite type, form X(R) with its semi-algebraic site (semi-algebraic opens, admissible finite covers); obtain X(C) by gluing Weil restrictions of affine charts. Complex conjugation acts with fixed locus X(R).

api.name: RealCycles.semialgebraicSite.characterise
api.statement: Restriction to affine charts recovers polynomial equalities and inequalities over R.

api.name: RealCycles.semialgebraicSite.compatibility
api.statement: The fixed-point inclusion identifies X(R) with X(C)^G.

api.name: RealCycles.semialgebraicSite.functoriality
api.statement: Base extension between real closed fields preserves the relevant semialgebraic cohomology after the transfer theorem, not by a homeomorphism assertion.

api.name: RealCycles.equivariantSupports.compatibility

items.name: Parity twist of coefficients
items.statement: For a G-module M and j∈Z set M(j)=M⊗Z Z(j), where Z(j)=i^j Z with conjugation multiplication by (−1)^j; use the same notation for the associated equivariant locally constant sheaf.

api.name: RealCycles.twist.characterise
api.statement: M(j)(k) identifies coherently with M(j+k).

api.name: RealCycles.twist.compatibility
api.statement: The forgetful abelian group is M, but the G-action changes when j is odd.

api.name: RealCycles.twist.functoriality
api.statement: Tensor products add twists and reductions modulo two forget the sign action.

items.name: Real-complex coefficient exact sequences
items.statement: For every G-module M, the augmentation/twisted-diagonal maps give 0→M→M[G]→M(1)→0 and its twist 0→M(1)→M[G]→M→0; the associated cohomology sequences identify the middle term with ordinary cohomology and its map back with norm.

items.name: Fundamental sign class
items.statement: Define ω∈H¹(G,Z(1)) as the boundary of 1 in the real-complex sequence and pull it back to every G-space. For any coefficient M, that sequence's boundary is cup product with ω; 2ω=0.

api.name: RealCycles.omega.characterise
api.statement: Pullback carries ω to ω.

api.name: RealCycles.omega.compatibility
api.statement: Connecting maps are cup-ω, with the specified twist increment.

api.name: RealCycles.omega.functoriality
api.statement: For i≥0 define ω^i, retaining ω^0=1 rather than treating it as torsion.

items.statement: For ρ:V→V/G, form the group-cohomology sheaves H^q(G,F) on V/G and E2^{p,q}=H^p_{ρ(Z)}(V/G,H^q(G,F))⇒H^{p+q}_{G,Z}(V,F).

api.name: RealCycles.quotientSpectral.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.quotientSpectral.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.quotientSpectral.functoriality

items.name: Torsion semi-algebraic–étale comparison
items.statement: For X/R a variety and a torsion G-module M, H^i_G(X(C),M) canonically identifies with H^i_et(X,M); for ℓ-adic coefficients the integral semialgebraic groups compare after completion under the finite-generation hypotheses used in §1.1.1.
items.note: Precise inverse-limit/derived-limit proof remains GAP-COMPARE; no arbitrary integral étale equality is asserted.

items.name: Comparison over actual real numbers
items.statement: When R=ℝ, semialgebraic cohomology of X(ℝ), and equivariant cohomology of X(ℂ), agrees with the ordinary singular/Borel version with the same locally constant coefficients and supports.

items.name: Relative cohomology of the real-locus pair
items.statement: For j:U=X(C)\X(R)→X(C), define HG^i(X(C),X(R);M)=HG^i(X(C),j!M|U). This is not HG^i with support X(R); it has its own localization long exact sequence.

api.name: RealCycles.relativeReal.characterise
api.statement: Map relative cohomology to absolute then to real-locus cohomology.

api.name: RealCycles.relativeReal.compatibility
api.statement: Compare relative cohomology with compact support on the quotient when X is proper.

api.name: RealCycles.relativeReal.functoriality
api.statement: The free complement U/G carries the descended coefficient local system.

items.name: Free-action descent and dimension bounds
items.statement: For a free semialgebraic G-action, equivariant cohomology equals cohomology of the quotient with the descended sheaf. api.name: RealCycles.orientation.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.orientation.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.orientation.functoriality

items.name: Semi-algebraic exceptional inverse image
items.statement: For a semialgebraic map f between locally complete spaces, construct f! on the derived sheaf category as right adjoint to Rf_! using proper supports, with unit/counit and composition; use the concrete semialgebraic site rather than importing an étale f! without comparison.

api.name: RealCycles.semialgExceptional.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.semialgExceptional.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.semialgExceptional.functoriality

items.name: Orientation formula for exceptional inverse image
items.statement: If f:V→W is a semialgebraic map between locally complete homology manifolds of pure dimensions v,w, Λ is noetherian and F is a bounded complex of Λ-sheaves with locally constant cohomology, then Rf!F≅or_{V/W}⊗_Z f*F[v−w].

items.name: Cup product as derived composition
items.statement: For bounded-above sheaf complexes A1,A2, degree-zero classes x_i represented by φ_i:Z→A_i have cup product represented by (Id⊗φ2)∘φ1:Z→A1⊗^L A2.

items.name: Semi-algebraic Gysin and trace
items.statement: For a proper f:V→W of homology manifolds and c=dim W−dim V, the counit and orientation formula define f_*:H^i(V,or_{V/W}⊗f*F)→H^{i+c}(W,F). For a closed embedding the support-valued map is the purity isomorphism.

api.name: RealCycles.gysin.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.gysin.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.gysin.functoriality
api.statement: f_*(α∪f*β)=f_*α∪β with the stated twists and degrees.

items.name: Finite-coefficient Poincaré duality

items.name: Finite-dimensional Borel approximation
items.statement: Let G act antipodally on S^n⊂R^{n+1}. For equivariant sheaf F on T and invariant closed Z, descend p*F to Fbar on (T×S^n)/G. For i<n, HG,Z^i(T,F)=H^i_{(Z×S^n)/G}((T×S^n)/G,Fbar).

api.name: RealCycles.finiteBorel.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.finiteBorel.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.finiteBorel.functoriality
api.statement: Ordinary constant F need not descend to a constant sheaf when its G-action is nontrivial.

items.name: Equivariant purity and proper pushforward
items.statement: Using finite Borel approximations, define equivariant purity for a closed embedding of codimension c and proper pushforward with relative orientation. For algebraic f:Y→X between smooth pure dimensions d',d, f_*:HG^i(Y(C),M(d'−d))→HG^{i+2(d−d')}(X(C),M).

api.name: RealCycles.equivariantGysin.compatibility

items.statement: For G=C2, H^q(G,Z(j)) is F2 if q>0 and q≡j mod2, zero if q≢j mod2, and Z if q=0 and j is even. H^*(G,F2)=F2[ωbar], with ωbar in degree one.

items.name: Canonical mod-two fixed-locus decomposition
items.statement: For i≥0, HG^i(X(R),F2)≅⊕_{p=0}^i H^p(X(R),F2), canonically and naturally. Under it, cup products are convolution (x∪y)_r=Σ_{p+q=r}x_p∪y_q.

api.name: RealCycles.mod2Decomposition.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.mod2Decomposition.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.mod2Decomposition.functoriality

items.name: Real-complex maps in mod-two coordinates
items.statement: On fixed-locus mod-two cohomology, forget equivariance is top-degree projection, norm is zero, and the connecting map is the inclusion ⊕_{p≤i}H^p→⊕_{p≤i+1}H^p; ωbar^i has coordinate 1 in H⁰ and zero elsewhere.

items.name: Real proper pushforward in coordinates
items.statement: For a proper f:Y→X between smooth equidimensional varieties and c=dim X−dim Y, the fixed-locus equivariant pushforward in mod-two coordinates is the direct sum of f_*:H^p(Y(R),F2)→H^{p+c}(X(R),F2).

items.name: Real-locus self-intersection class
items.statement: For smooth pure-d-dimensional X/R, let γ∈⊕_{p=0}^dH^p(X(R),F2) be the restriction of the equivariant fundamental class of X(R)⊂X(C), decomposed in total equivariant degree d.

api.name: RealCycles.gamma.characterise
api.statement: Restriction after real-locus Gysin is multiplication by γ.

api.name: RealCycles.gamma.compatibility
api.statement: Its degree-zero coordinate is 1 and higher-degree part is nilpotent.

api.name: RealCycles.gamma.functoriality
api.statement: Its inverse is the finite geometric series in γ−1, truncated above dimension d.

items.name: Invertibility of the real-locus class
items.statement: For smooth X/R, γ has degree-zero part 1 and is invertible in ⊕H^p(X(R),F2). Under purity the support-to-absolute-to-real map is multiplication by γ followed by the natural inclusion in the larger degree window.

items.name: Canonical split mod-two support sequence
items.statement: For smooth X/R and i≥0, 0→HG,X(R)^i(X(C),F2)→HG^i(X(C),F2)→HG^i(X(C)\X(R),F2)→0 is exact and canonically split.

items.name: Stiefel–Whitney identification over ℝ
items.statement: For smooth X/ℝ, γ equals the total Stiefel–Whitney class w(TX(ℝ)). This is the normal/tangent identification used in the Wu pushforward formula.

items.name: Canonical classes separating real components
items.statement: For a semialgebraically connected component V of X(R), its support fundamental class yields an equivariant degree-d mod-two class whose evaluation at a real point is nonzero exactly on V; comparison gives the corresponding étale class.

items.name: Parity-restricted integral support splitting
items.statement: For smooth irreducible d-dimensional X/R, j≡d−1 mod2 and i≥0, 0→HG,X(R)^i(X(C),Z(j))→HG^i(X(C),Z(j))→HG^i(X(C)\X(R),Z(j))→0 is canonically split.

items.name: Surjectivity onto low real components
items.statement: For smooth irreducible d-dimensional X/R, i≥0 and j∈Z, restriction and decomposition surject onto ⊕_{0≤p<i−d,p≡i−j mod2}H^p(X(R),F2). The proof produces a canonical section through support cohomology.

items.name: Duality between relative and free-complement groups
items.statement: For smooth proper pure-d-dimensional X/R and a finite G-module M, relative equivariant cohomology of (X(C),X(R)) pairs perfectly with free-complement cohomology in degree 2d−i with coefficient Hom(M,Q/Z)(d), via trace to Q/Z.

items.name: Profinite integral duality
items.statement: For smooth proper pure-d-dimensional X/R and a finitely generated G-module M, the profinite completion of HG^i(X(C),X(R);M) identifies with the Pontryagin dual of HG^{2d−i}(X(C)\X(R),Hom(M,Q/Z(d))).
items.note: Passage through finite coefficients and finite generation are proof obligations; no algebraic self-duality of arbitrary abelian groups is asserted.

items.name: Real-locus corrected localization sequence
items.statement: For smooth proper irreducible d-dimensional X/R, quotient support localization to obtain ...→⊕_{p=i−d}^{i−1}H^p(X(R),F2) —u^i→ HG^i(X(C),X(R);F2) —v^i→ HG^i(U,F2) —w^i→⊕_{p=i−d+1}^{i}H^p(X(R),F2)→.... Here v is forget-relative then restrict; w is restrict, multiply by γ^−1 and project; u is multiply by γ, truncate to its input window, then the localization boundary.

api.name: RealCycles.selfdualLes.characterise
api.statement: Each consecutive composite vanishes and the sequence is exact.

api.name: RealCycles.selfdualLes.compatibility
api.statement: Windows include their specified endpoints; cohomology outside 0..d is zero.

api.name: RealCycles.selfdualLes.functoriality
api.statement: Pair complementary real blocks by deg(xyγ), not deg(xy) without γ.

items.name: Boundary trace formula
items.statement: For z∈⊕_{p=0}^{2d−1}H^p(X(R),F2), its image under the real-locus localization boundary and relative trace equals deg(zγ^−1).

items.name: Self-duality of corrected localization
items.statement: The corrected localization LES is self-dual: for every integer i, (u^i)^∨=w^{2d−i}, (v^i)^∨=v^{2d−i}, (w^i)^∨=u^{2d−i}, using relative/complement duality and the real-block pairing deg(xyγ).

items.name: High-degree restriction on an affine variety
items.statement: For affine U/R of dimension d, any G-module M and i>d, HG^i(U(C),M)→HG^i(U(R),M) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Real-empty equivariant weak Lefschetz
items.statement: If X/R is smooth projective of dimension d, X(R)=empty and Y⊂X is a smooth ample divisor, then Gysin HG^{i−2}(Y(C),M(−1))→HG^i(X(C),M) is an isomorphism for i>d+1 and surjective for i=d+1.

items.name: Weak Lefschetz with real-locus criterion
items.statement: Let X/R be smooth projective dimension d, Y a smooth ample divisor, i≥d+1 and j∈Z. If H^{p−1}(Y(R),F2)→H^p(X(R),F2) is surjective for every p≥1 with p≡i−j mod2, then the image of HG^{i−2}(Y(C),Z(j−1))→HG^i(X(C),Z(j)) is precisely the classes restricting to zero at every real point of X.

items.name: Injective weak Lefschetz variant
items.statement: In Proposition1.15's setting with i>d+1, if real Gysin is injective for p≥1 with p≡i−j mod2 and surjective for p≥1 of the opposite parity, then the integral equivariant complex Gysin is injective.

items.name: Affine relative vanishing with torsion coefficients
items.statement: For affine U/R of dimension d and a torsion G-module M, HG^i(U(C),U(R);M)=0 for i>d.

items.name: Integral equivariant cycle class
items.statement: For smooth X/R and codimension-k cycles, construct cl:CH^k(X)→HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)): start from the fundamental class on a dense smooth locus, extend uniquely using support vanishing, and prove rational equivalence maps to zero.

api.name: RealCycles.equivariantCycle.characterise
api.statement: The class of a smooth closed subvariety is its Gysin image of 1.

api.name: RealCycles.equivariantCycle.compatibility
api.statement: The map factors through rational equivalence and is additive.

api.name: RealCycles.equivariantCycle.functoriality
api.statement: Proper pushforward, pullback on smooth varieties and intersection products agree with cohomological pushforward, pullback and cup product.

items.name: Borel–Haefliger cycle class
items.statement: For smooth X/R, define cl_R:CH^k(X)→H^k(X(R),F2) from the mod-two fundamental classes of real loci of cycles, including singular cycles via supported extension. It respects products, pullbacks and proper pushforward.

api.name: RealCycles.bhCycle.characterise
api.statement: A smooth real codimension-k subvariety has its ordinary mod-two fundamental class.

api.name: RealCycles.bhCycle.compatibility
api.statement: Empty real support yields zero.

api.name: RealCycles.bhCycle.functoriality
api.statement: Cycle operations commute with the corresponding mod-two operations and degree shifts.

items.name: Algebraic cohomology of the real locus
items.statement: H_alg^k(X(R),F2) is the image of cl_R:CH^k(X)→H^k(X(R),F2), with CH_1 denoting CH^{d−1} in pure dimension d.

api.name: RealCycles.halg.characterise
api.statement: Membership is existence of an algebraic cycle with the specified real class.

api.name: RealCycles.halg.compatibility
api.statement: Proper pushforward and smooth pullback preserve algebraic classes.

api.name: RealCycles.halg.functoriality
api.statement: Equality H_alg^k=H^k is exactly surjectivity of the real cycle map.

items.name: Semi-algebraic Steenrod operations
items.statement: Construct mod-two Steenrod squares Sq^i:H^k(V,F2)→H^{k+i}(V,F2) on semialgebraic spaces, with Sq^0=Id, Sq^i=0 for i<0 or i>k, Sq^k(x)=x², Cartan, naturality and Adem relations; total Sq is invertible on finite-dimensional cohomology as an ungraded filtered operator.

api.name: RealCycles.steenrod.characterise
api.statement: Total Sq has inverse by finite-degree triangularity.

api.name: RealCycles.steenrod.compatibility
api.statement: Sq¹ is the ordinary Bockstein and Sq^{2m+1}=Sq¹Sq^{2m}.

api.name: RealCycles.steenrod.functoriality
api.statement: Cartan makes total Sq multiplicative, not degree-preserving.

items.name: Kahn–Krasnov constraints on algebraic classes
items.statement: For smooth X/R, a codimension-k cycle Y and α=cl(Y), the fixed-locus components satisfy α_{k+i}=Sq^i(cl_R(Y)) for every even integer i, including negative i with Sq^i=0.

items.name: Topologically admissible integral classes
items.statement: Define HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0 as the subgroup of α satisfying α_{k+i}=Sq^i(α_k) for every even i. Its real component map is α↦α_k, and cl_R factors through it via the integral cycle class.

api.name: RealCycles.topologicalSubgroup.characterise
api.statement: Membership is the complete even-square component condition, not only vanishing at real points.

api.name: RealCycles.topologicalSubgroup.compatibility
api.statement: The real-component map is additive on this subgroup.

api.name: RealCycles.topologicalSubgroup.functoriality
api.statement: Cup products and pullbacks preserve the subgroup, with the correct codimension.

items.name: All-square mod-two characterization
items.statement: An integral class α lies in HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0 iff its mod-two restriction components satisfy αbar_{k+i}=Sq^i(αbar_k) for every integer i, using 1+β for coefficient reduction and the Adem relation.

items.name: Integral lift of an even-degree square
items.statement: If k is even and α∈HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0, then α_k² lies in the image H^{2k}(X(R),Z)→H^{2k}(X(R),F2).

items.name: Steenrod-conjugated restriction of proper pushforward
items.statement: For a proper f:Y→X between smooth irreducible varieties, restriction of equivariant mod-two pushforward in fixed-locus coordinates is Sq∘f_*∘Sq^−1, with the degree windows and complex/real dimension shifts of Proposition1.22. Equivalently it is γ_X·f_*(γ_Y^−1·−).

items.name: Proper pushforward preserves admissible classes
items.statement: For proper f:Y→X between smooth irreducible varieties of dimensions d',d, f_* sends HG^{2k}(Y(C),Z(k))_0 into HG^{2(k+d−d')}(X(C),Z(k+d−d'))_0, and its real-component map equals real Gysin on H^k(Y(R),F2).

items.name: Integral Hodge classes and conjecture
items.statement: For smooth proper X/ℂ, Hdg^{2k}(X,Z(k)) is the subgroup of integral classes whose complexification has Hodge type (k,k), including torsion classes. Integral HC means surjectivity of CH^k(X)→Hdg^{2k}; rational HC only asserts surjectivity after tensoring Q.

api.name: RealCycles.integralHodge.characterise
api.statement: Torsion integral cohomology classes satisfy the Hodge-type condition.

api.name: RealCycles.integralHodge.compatibility
api.statement: Integral and rational defects are separate quotients.

api.name: RealCycles.integralHodge.functoriality
api.statement: For 1-cycles the group is in degree 2d−2 and twist d−1.

items.name: Real integral Hodge subgroup
items.statement: For smooth proper X/ℝ, define Hdg_G^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0 as HG^{2k}_0 intersected with the inverse image of Hdg^{2k}(X(C),Z(k)) under forgetting equivariance. Real integral HC is surjectivity of the equivariant cycle map onto this subgroup.

api.name: RealCycles.realHodge.characterise
api.statement: Membership combines the complex Hodge condition with the full real topological condition.

api.name: RealCycles.realHodge.compatibility
api.statement: The equivariant cycle class factors through the subgroup.

api.name: RealCycles.realHodge.functoriality
api.statement: Its cokernel measures real integral HC, not merely surjectivity onto G-invariants.

items.name: Real-closed-field integral Hodge property
items.statement: For smooth proper X/R and k≥0, assume H^q(X,Ω_X^p)=0 whenever p+q=2k and (p,q)≠(k,k). Define real integral HC in codimension k as CH^k(X)↠HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0. Do not posit an analytic Hodge decomposition over arbitrary R.

api.name: RealCycles.realclosedHodge.characterise
api.statement: Record off-diagonal vanishing as a hypothesis, not as part of a phantom Hodge structure.

api.name: RealCycles.realclosedHodge.compatibility
api.statement: For 1-cycles H²(X,O_X)=0 supplies the needed vanishing by duality.

api.name: RealCycles.realclosedHodge.functoriality
api.statement: When R=ℝ and vanishing holds, this agrees with Definition2.2.

items.name: Norm comparison for rational Hodge classes
items.statement: For smooth proper X/ℝ, if X_C satisfies rational HC in codimension k, then the real equivariant cycle class map to Hdg_G^{2k}_0 becomes surjective after tensoring Q.

items.name: Positive constant classes and real emptiness
items.statement: For smooth proper X/R and positive even k, identify Z(2k) with Z(k). The class ω^{2k} belongs to HG^{2k}_0 iff X(R)=empty; over ℝ it is Hodge because it is torsion.
items.note: Printed text says k≥0 even. Exclude k=0: ω⁰=1 is non-torsion and admissible with real points. This is a source-boundary correction, not a silent restatement.

items.name: Anisotropic quadric constant-class obstruction
items.statement: For the smooth projective anisotropic quadric X/R of dimension n, ω⁴ is algebraic iff −1 is a sum of seven squares in R(X), iff n≤6. Thus real integral HC for codimension two fails when n≥7.

items.name: Real integral Lefschetz (1,1)
items.statement: Every smooth proper variety over ℝ satisfies real integral HC for divisors.

items.name: Torsion-free divisor cycle-class cokernel
items.statement: For smooth X over a real closed field R, the cokernel of cl:Pic(X)→HG²(X(C),Z(1)) is torsion-free.

items.name: Divisor surjectivity under H²(O)=0
items.statement: For smooth proper X/R with H²(X,O_X)=0, Pic(X)→HG²(X(C),Z(1)) is surjective and hence real integral HC for divisors holds.

items.name: Top complex cohomology generated by points
items.statement: For smooth proper pure-d-dimensional X/R, sending each connected component of X_C to a closed-point class gives Z^{π0(X_C)}≅H^{2d}(X(C),Z(d)).

items.name: Norm exact sequence in top degree
items.statement: For smooth proper pure-d-dimensional X/R, the norm has image in HG^{2d}_0 and H^{2d}(X(C),Z(d))→HG^{2d}(X(C),Z(d))_0→H^d(X(R),F2)→0 is exact; if X is geometrically connected the norm is injective.

items.name: Real integral Hodge conjecture for zero-cycles
items.statement: Every smooth proper pure-d-dimensional variety over R satisfies real integral HC for zero-cycles: CH^d(X)↠HG^{2d}(X(C),Z(d))_0.

items.name: Orthogonality for a complex-null factor
items.statement: For smooth proper pure-d-dimensional X/R, if admissible complementary-degree classes α,β have one complex forgetful class zero, then their real components have zero mod-two intersection degree.

items.name: Blowup decomposition of admissible classes
items.statement: For smooth X/R, smooth irreducible center Z of codimension r and blowup π:Xtilde→X with exceptional i:E→Xtilde, τ:E→Z and ξ=cl(O_E(1)), the map (α,(β_j))↦π*α+Σ_{j=k−r+1}^{k−1}i_*(ξ^{k−j−1}τ*β_j) is an isomorphism HG^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0⊕⊕_j HG^{2j}(Z(C),Z(j))_0≅HG^{2k}(Xtilde(C),Z(k))_0.

items.name: Blowup decomposition of real Hodge classes
items.statement: Over ℝ, the same blowup map restricts to the direct-sum isomorphism of Hdg_G^{2k}_0 and its center summands Hdg_G^{2j}_0.

items.name: Birational invariance of real Hodge defects
items.statement: For smooth proper pure-d-dimensional X/ℝ and k∈{2,d−1}, Coker(CH^k(X)→Hdg_G^{2k}(X(C),Z(k))_0) is birationally invariant.

items.name: Birational invariance of the 1-cycle topological defect
items.statement: Over every real closed R, Coker(CH^{d−1}(X)→HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0) is birationally invariant among smooth proper pure-d-dimensional varieties.

items.name: Real integral Hodge property of projective space
items.statement: For every real closed R and 0≤k≤d, CH^k(P^d_R)→HG^{2k}(P^d(C),Z(k))_0 is surjective.

items.name: Genus detector without real points
items.statement: Under S3 and X(R)=empty, put M=F2. Define ψ:HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0→M by cup with ω² followed by HG^{2d}(X(C),Z(d+1))≅F2. Define ψ':Pic(X_C)^G[2∞]→M*=F2 as the line-bundle descent obstruction in Br(R).

api.name: RealCycles.psiEmpty.characterise
api.statement: The top identification is the duality normalization, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

api.name: RealCycles.psiEmpty.compatibility
api.statement: A G-invariant line bundle has obstruction zero precisely when it descends to X.

api.name: RealCycles.psiEmpty.functoriality
api.statement: The obstruction group Br(R) is identified with F2.

items.name: Real-locus detector with real points
items.statement: Under S3 and X(R) nonempty, set M=H^{d−1}(X(R),F2). Define ψ as α↦α_{d−1}, and ψ':Pic(X_C)^G[2∞]=Pic(X)[2∞]→M*=H¹(X(R),F2) as the Borel–Haefliger map, using mod-two Poincaré duality.

api.name: RealCycles.psiReal.characterise
api.statement: The real point makes the Picard descent obstruction vanish.

api.name: RealCycles.psiReal.compatibility
api.statement: The dual pairing is cup product followed by total real degree.

api.name: RealCycles.psiReal.functoriality
api.statement: ψ agrees with cl_R after the integral cycle map.

items.name: Picard torsion image as cohomological restriction

items.name: Admissible 1-cycle classes on the free complement
items.statement: Under S3, restriction induces HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0≅HG^{2d−2}(X(C)\X(R),Z(d−1)).

items.name: Exact orthogonality of the two detectors
items.statement: Under S3, Im ψ and Im ψ' are exact orthogonal complements under M×M*→F2, with ψ,ψ' defined separately in the real-empty and real-nonempty cases.

items.name: Cycle-theoretic real/genus detector
items.statement: Under S3, define φ:CH_1(X)→M by ψ∘cl. When X(R) is nonempty it is cl_R; when X(R) is empty it is the parity-of-normalization-Euler-characteristic detector.

api.name: RealCycles.phi.characterise
api.statement: φ is additive and factors through rational equivalence.

api.name: RealCycles.phi.compatibility
api.statement: Proper pushforward is compatible with the relevant detector on normalized curves.

api.name: RealCycles.phi.functoriality
api.statement: For no real points, an integral curve with even geometric genus contributes only when geometrically irreducible.

items.name: Cycle detector with real points
items.statement: Under S3 and X(R) nonempty, φ:CH_1(X)→H^{d−1}(X(R),F2) equals the Borel–Haefliger cycle class map.

items.name: Even-genus interpretation
items.statement: Under S3 and X(R)=empty, φ([B])=1 for an integral closed curve B⊂X iff B is geometrically irreducible and the genus of its smooth proper normalization is even; all other integral curves map to zero.

items.name: Geyer descent criterion for a curve
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve B/R with B(R)=empty, Pic(B_C)^G[2∞]→Br(R)=F2 is surjective iff the genus of B is even.

items.name: Geyer parity descent sublemma
items.statement: Let B/R be a smooth proper geometrically integral genus-g curve with no real point. Any G-invariant line bundle L on B_C with deg L≡g mod2 descends to B.

items.name: Existence of odd-genus curves
items.statement: A smooth proper geometrically irreducible variety of dimension at least two over an infinite perfect field contains a geometrically irreducible curve of odd geometric genus.

items.name: Even-genus curve through a real-point construction
items.statement: A smooth proper geometrically irreducible X/R of dimension at least two with X(R) nonempty contains a geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus.

items.name: Intermediate Euler-characteristic index
items.statement: For a proper variety X/k and i≥0, ind_i(X) is the nonnegative generator of the ideal of Z generated by χ(X,F) for coherent sheaves F whose support has dimension at most i. For nonempty X, ind_0 is the usual closed-point degree index and ind_d divides ... divides ind_0.

api.name: RealCycles.elwIndex.characterise
api.statement: A coherent sheaf with support dimension≤i contributes its Euler characteristic.

api.name: RealCycles.elwIndex.compatibility
api.statement: Increasing i can only enlarge the ideal and divide the positive generator.

api.name: RealCycles.elwIndex.functoriality
api.statement: Proper pushforward and Euler-characteristic devissage give functorial divisibility.

items.name: Computing intermediate indices by integral subvarieties
items.statement: For proper X/k and i≥0, ind_i(X) is the gcd of χ(Z,O_Z) for integral closed subvarieties Z⊂X of dimension≤i, and also the gcd of the corresponding normalization Euler characteristics.

items.name: First index and even-genus curves over R
items.statement: For nonempty proper X/R, ind_1(X)=1 iff X(R) is nonempty or X contains a geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus; otherwise ind_1(X)=2.

items.name: Euler characteristic under a finite curve map
items.statement: For a finite surjective map f:E→F of integral proper curves over a field, χ(E,O_E)−deg(f)χ(F,O_F) is divisible by ind_0(F).

items.name: Parity of genus under finite covers
items.statement: For a finite morphism E→F between smooth proper geometrically irreducible curves over R, if F(R)=empty and F has even genus, then E has even genus iff deg(E/F) is odd.

items.name: Euler characteristic modulo lower index
items.statement: For smooth proper X/k, χ of normalizations of dimension-i integral subvarieties induces CH_i(X)→Z/ind_{i−1}(X), and factors through algebraic equivalence. For k real closed and i=1 it also factors through the equivariant homological cycle class via φ.

api.name: RealCycles.eulerCycleMap.characterise
api.statement: Different representatives of rationally equivalent cycles have the same residue.

api.name: RealCycles.eulerCycleMap.compatibility
api.statement: Algebraic families preserve this residue modulo the lower index.

api.name: RealCycles.eulerCycleMap.functoriality
api.statement: The real i=1 homological factorization is separate from the general-field algebraic-equivalence assertion.

items.name: Odd-order penultimate complex cohomology
items.statement: Under S3 with Pic(X_C)[2]=0, H^{2d−1}(X(C),Z) is finite of odd order.

items.name: Cup-ω quotient near top degree
items.statement: Under S3 with Pic(X_C)[2]=0, cup-ω maps HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1)) onto HG^{2d−1}(X(C),Z(d))[2], with kernel the image of the ordinary-to-equivariant norm.

items.name: Cup-ω on top 2-torsion
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, cup-ω gives HG^{2d−1}(X(C),Z(d))[2]≅HG^{2d}(X(C),Z(d+1)).

items.name: Cup-ω above top degree with a real point
items.statement: Under S3, Pic(X_C)[2]=0 and X(R) nonempty, cup-ω gives HG^{2d}(X(C),Z(d+1))≅HG^{2d+1}(X(C),Z(d+2)).

items.name: Norm-detector exact sequence without Picard 2-torsion
items.statement: Under S3 with Pic(X_C)[2]=0, H^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1)) —Norm→ HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0 —ψ→ M→0 is exact; norm lands in the admissible subgroup.

items.name: Topological, Hodge and cycle obstructions
items.statement: Under S3, a topological obstruction means ψ is not onto. Over ℝ a Hodge obstruction means ψ is onto but its restriction to real Hodge classes is not. A cycle obstruction means the applicable preceding obstruction vanishes but φ is not onto (use H²(O_X)=0 over general R).

api.name: RealCycles.obstructionTypes.characterise
api.statement: The predicates distinguish failure at the three successive maps.

api.name: RealCycles.obstructionTypes.compatibility
api.statement: No Pic(X_C)[2] means no topological obstruction by the norm-detector sequence.

api.name: RealCycles.obstructionTypes.functoriality
api.statement: A cycle obstruction implies failure of the real integral Hodge property, but its converse is not asserted.

items.name: Algebraic 1-cycle and Picard torsion orthogonality
items.statement: Under S3, H²(X,O_X)=0 and real integral HC for 1-cycles, cl_R(CH_1(X)) and cl_R(Pic(X)[2∞]) are exact orthogonal complements in H^{d−1}(X(R),F2) and H¹(X(R),F2).

items.name: Even-genus equivalence with verified dimension scope
items.statement: Assume S3, H²(X,O_X)=0, real integral HC for 1-cycles, and additionally d≥2 OR X(R)=empty. Then X contains a geometrically irreducible even-geometric-genus curve iff Pic(X)[2∞]→Pic(X_C)^G[2∞] is onto.

items.name: Surjectivity of real cycle classes without Picard 2-torsion

items.name: Even genus without Picard 2-torsion
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, X contains a geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus, including d=1.

items.name: Geometric-genus-zero surface orthogonality
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically irreducible surface X/R with H²(X,O_X)=0, H_alg¹(X(R),F2) and cl_R(Pic(X)[2∞]) are exact orthogonal complements.

items.name: Even-genus criterion for geometric-genus-zero surfaces
items.statement: For the same surface, an even-geometric-genus geometrically irreducible curve exists iff Pic(X)[2∞]→Pic(X_C)^G[2∞] is onto.

items.name: Enriques Picard torsion input
items.statement: For an Enriques surface X over a real closed field, H²(X,O_X)=0 and Pic(X_C)[2∞] is generated by its canonical class, which is the pullback of K_X∈Pic(X)[2].

items.name: Even-genus curve on every real Enriques surface
items.statement: Every Enriques surface over a real closed field contains a geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus.

items.name: Half-dimension lower bound
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically irreducible surface X/R with H²(O_X)=0, dim_F2 H_alg¹(X(R),F2)≥(1/2)dim_F2 H¹(X(R),F2); in particular H¹ nonzero implies H_alg¹ nonzero.

items.name: Sharp conic-bundle example
items.statement: If E/R is an elliptic curve with two real components and X→E is a conic-bundle surface smooth above E(R) with X(R) connected and nonempty, then dim H¹(X(R),F2)=2 and dim H_alg¹(X(R),F2)=1.

items.name: Criterion from complex integral Hodge theory
items.statement: Under S3, H²(O_X)=0 and Pic(X_C)[2]=0, assume X_C satisfies integral HC for 1-cycles (the algebraicity formulation over arbitrary R). Then X satisfies real integral HC for 1-cycles iff φ is onto: equivalently H_alg^{d−1}=H^{d−1} when real points exist, and existence of a geometrically irreducible even-genus curve when they do not.

items.name: Rationally connected and simply connected Calabi–Yau threefolds
items.statement: For a smooth proper threefold X/R that is geometrically rationally connected, or is geometrically simply connected Calabi–Yau (K trivial, H¹(O)=H²(O)=0), real integral HC for 1-cycles holds iff H_alg²(X(R),F2)=H²(X(R),F2) when X(R) is nonempty, and iff X contains an even-genus geometrically irreducible curve when X(R) is empty.

items.name: Disconnected real curve obstruction
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve X/R with at least two real connected components, the image of CH_1(X) in H⁰(X(R),F2) consists of constant functions, so φ is not onto.

items.name: Odd-genus no-real curve obstruction
items.statement: A smooth proper geometrically irreducible odd-genus curve X/R with X(R)=empty has ind_1(X)=2.

items.name: Nonorientable Enriques obstruction
items.statement: For a real Enriques surface with nonorientable real locus, H_alg¹(X(R),F2) is a proper subgroup of H¹(X(R),F2); the obstruction is topological.

items.name: Displayed antilinear cyclic action on projective space
items.statement: Over ℂ choose primitive eighth root ζ and define f on P⁶ by [x0:...:x6]↦[ζ conjugate(x1):conjugate(x0):ζ² conjugate(x3):conjugate(x2):ζ³ conjugate(x5):conjugate(x4):conjugate(x6)]. Then <f>=C16 with holomorphic subgroup <f²>=C8. Use four quadrics from the ζ^{2i} eigenspaces of (f²)* on H⁰(O(2)), i=0..3, with the specified lift to O(1).

api.name: RealCycles.campedelliAction.characterise
api.statement: Compute f² as the diagonal action and verify f has order sixteen.

api.name: RealCycles.campedelliAction.compatibility
api.statement: The eigenspace labels depend on the lift sending x0 to ζx0.

api.name: RealCycles.campedelliAction.functoriality
api.statement: f⁸ fixes the union of P³ on coordinates0,1,4,5 and P² on coordinates2,3,6. Every nontrivial subgroup of C16 contains f⁸, so avoiding this union would imply freeness; existence of the prescribed stable surface is impossible by E3.

items.name: Obstruction to the displayed Campedelli descent
items.statement: There is no f-stable smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection surface in P⁶ cut out by one Qi∈Λ_i for each i=0,1,2,3 with f and its lift as printed in Example4.4. Thus that displayed construction cannot supply the asserted real-empty surface. The broader existence claim requires a replacement construction and is not refuted by this statement.
items.note: Corrects the previous positive existence item, retaining its stable ID. This extraction supplies a mathematical obstruction, not an independent review verdict. No conclusion about all real Campedelli surfaces follows.

items.name: Real quartic surface with a Hodge obstruction
items.statement: A very general sufficiently small real deformation of a smooth real quartic surface containing a real line can have Pic(X_C)=Z·O_X(1) while retaining the transported real line cohomology class. Hyperplane self-intersection has even degree, but pairing that class with the hyperplane is odd; hence H_alg¹(X(R),F2)≠H¹(X(R),F2), a Hodge obstruction.

items.name: Real-empty very general quartic surface
items.statement: For a very general smooth quartic X⊂P³_ℝ with no real points, Pic(X_C)=Z·O_X(1), and X contains no geometrically irreducible curve of even geometric genus.

items.name: Odd-degree obstruction in the quartic generic fiber
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k, the quartic x0⁴+t x1⁴+t² x2⁴+t³ x3⁴=0 over k((t)) has no point over an odd-degree finite extension: the four finite valuations are distinct modulo four. Thus every curve in the corresponding special P¹×P³ hypersurface has even degree over P¹.
items.locator: Totaro2013 published Theorem3.1 proof (author preprint Theorem2.1), pp.4–5

items.name: Even-degree persistence under specialization
items.statement: For a smooth characteristic-zero hypersurface specializing to u³x0⁴+tu²x1⁴+t²ux2⁴+t³x3⁴=0 over a finite field, every complex curve has even projection degree. Multiplying the special equation by the other base coordinate to obtain bidegree (4,4) leaves the generic-fiber obstruction unchanged; vertical components have projection degree zero.

items.name: Cycle obstruction with real points
items.statement: There exists a smooth bidegree-(4,4) hypersurface X⊂P¹_Q×P³_Q for which projection H_1(X(ℝ),F2)→H_1(P¹(ℝ),F2) is onto, but every complex curve has even projection degree, so H_alg²(X(ℝ),F2)≠H²(X(ℝ),F2). Here H²(X,O_X)=0 and Pic(X_C)[2]=0, so the obstruction is cycle-theoretic.

items.name: Cycle obstruction without real points
items.statement: There exists a smooth bidegree-(4,4) hypersurface over an anisotropic real conic B defined over Q times P³, with H²(O_X)=0 and Pic(X_C)[2]=0, such that X(ℝ)=empty and ind_1(X)=2; hence it has no geometrically irreducible even-genus curve.

items.name: Coniveau filtration by algebraic support
items.statement: For smooth X/R, G-module M and p≥0, N^p HG^i(X(C),M) consists of classes supported on Z(C) for some Zariski closed Z⊂X of codimension at least p; use N^p=HG for p≤0.

api.name: RealCycles.coniveau.characterise
api.statement: N^0 is the full group and N^{p+1}⊆N^p.

api.name: RealCycles.coniveau.compatibility
api.statement: Purity shifts degree by twice codimension and twists by minus codimension.

api.name: RealCycles.coniveau.functoriality
api.statement: A coefficient morphism, including a boundary of theories with supports, preserves coniveau.

items.name: Zariski cohomology sheaves
items.statement: For smooth X/R and G-module M, H_X^q(M) is the Zariski sheafification of U↦HG^q(U(C),M). For X_C use ordinary cohomology. Its sections at the generic point are filtered colimits over dense opens.

api.statement: Restrictions are induced by open immersions before sheafification.

api.name: RealCycles.cohomologySheaf.compatibility

api.name: RealCycles.cohomologySheaf.functoriality

items.name: Induced-coefficient cohomology sheaf
items.statement: For π:X_C→X and any G-module M, H_X^q(M[G])≅π_*H_{X_C}^q(M).

items.name: Zariski cohomology after complexification
items.statement: For all p,q≥0 and M, H^p_Zar(X,π_*H_{X_C}^q(M))≅H^p_Zar(X_C,H_{X_C}^q(M)).

items.name: Torsion-free near-diagonal integral cohomology sheaves
items.statement: For smooth X/R and q≥0, both H_X^q(Z(q−1)) and H_X^q(Z[G]) are torsion-free.

items.name: High cohomology sheaves are real-evaluation sheaves
items.statement: For smooth d-dimensional X/R, q>d and any G-module M, H_X^q(M)≅ι_*H^q(G,M), where ι is the morphism from the semialgebraic real-locus site to the Zariski site.

items.name: High cohomology sheaf groups on the real locus
items.statement: In the same setting, H^p_Zar(X,H_X^q(M))≅H^p(X(R),H^q(G,M)) for all p≥0, using exactness of ι_* on the relevant real-site sheaves.

items.name: Coniveau quotient detected by low real components
items.statement: For smooth d-dimensional X/R, i≥0 and j∈Z, HG^i(X(C),Z(j))/N^{i−d}≅⊕_{0≤p<i−d,p≡i−j mod2}H^p(X(R),F2), induced by restriction and decomposition.

items.name: Vanishing of higher differentials above the dimension
items.statement: For the equivariant coniveau spectral sequence of smooth d-dimensional X/R and any G-module M, d_r^{p,q}=0 for r≥2 and q>d.

items.name: Cohomology sheaf with zero real evaluation
items.statement: For q≥0, define H_X^q(M)_0=ker(H_X^q(M)→ι_*H^q(G,M)), the subsheaf with zero evaluation at all real points.

api.name: RealCycles.zeroRealSheaf.characterise
api.statement: The kernel is formed in abelian Zariski sheaves.

api.name: RealCycles.zeroRealSheaf.compatibility
api.statement: If X(R)=empty it is the whole cohomology sheaf.

api.name: RealCycles.zeroRealSheaf.functoriality
api.statement: For q>dim X it is zero by the high-real-sheaf theorem.

items.name: Universal surface support of zero-cycles
items.statement: For proper X/R, the hypothesis means: for every algebraically closed extension C'/R there is a closed subvariety of X_C' of dimension at most two whose CH0 pushes onto CH0(X_C'). It is not merely support for the single field C=R(i).

api.name: RealCycles.universalCh0Support.characterise
api.statement: Apply the hypothesis after further algebraically closed extensions.

api.name: RealCycles.universalCh0Support.compatibility
api.statement: A universally CH0-trivial or geometrically rationally connected smooth proper variety has point support after supplying its proof.

api.name: RealCycles.universalCh0Support.functoriality

items.name: Rational coniveau-sheaf vanishing from universal support
items.statement: For smooth proper geometrically irreducible d-dimensional X/R with universal surface support, H^{d−3}(X_C,H_{X_C}^d(Q))=0, hence H^{d−3}(X,H_X^d(Q(d−1)))=0.

items.name: Integral-rational-torsion exact sequence with real evaluation
items.statement: For smooth d-dimensional X/R, 0→H_X^d(Z(d−1))→H_X^d(Q(d−1))→H_X^d(Q/Z(d−1))_0→0 is exact.

items.name: Highest coniveau equals algebraic 1-cycle image
items.statement: For smooth proper d-dimensional X/R, N^{d−1}HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1)) is the image of CH_1(X).

items.name: Next coniveau equals admissible 1-cycle classes
items.statement: For smooth proper d-dimensional X/R, N^{d−2}HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))=HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0.

items.name: Whole 1-cycle defect as sheaf cohomology
items.statement: For smooth proper geometrically irreducible d-dimensional X/R, Coker(CH_1(X)→HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0)≅H^{d−2}(X,H_X^d(Z(d−1))).

items.name: Unramified description of the torsion defect
items.statement: For smooth proper geometrically irreducible d-dimensional X/R with universal surface support, H^{d−3}(X,H_X^d(Q/Z(d−1))_0)≅Coker(CH_1(X)→HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0)_tors.

items.name: Vanishing criterion for real integral Hodge theory
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of the previous item, and R=ℝ or H²(O_X)=0, real integral HC for 1-cycles is equivalent to H^{d−3}(X,H_X^d(Q/Z(d−1))_0)=0.

items.name: Bloch Abel–Jacobi map for torsion 1-cycles
items.statement: For smooth proper irreducible d-dimensional X/R, construct λ:CH_1(X)_tors→H_et^{2d−3}(X,Q/Z(d−1)), identified with equivariant cohomology by comparison. Its coefficient boundary equals the integral equivariant cycle class.

api.name: RealCycles.blochAj.characterise
api.statement: λ is an additive map on actual torsion cycles.

api.name: RealCycles.blochAj.compatibility
api.statement: The composite with the coefficient boundary is cl.

api.name: RealCycles.blochAj.functoriality
api.statement: The target is in degree 2d−3, not the usual complex intermediate Jacobian itself.

items.statement: Define HG^{2d−3}(X(C),Q/Z(d−1))_0 as the inverse image of HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1))_0 under the boundary of 0→Z→Q→Q/Z→0.

api.name: RealCycles.ajAdmissible.characterise

api.name: RealCycles.ajAdmissible.compatibility
api.statement: Its definition is a boundary preimage, not pointwise real evaluation of the torsion class.

api.name: RealCycles.ajAdmissible.functoriality
api.statement: When X(R)=empty the subgroup is the full target.

items.name: Coniveau image of Bloch's map
items.statement: For smooth proper irreducible d-dimensional X/R, the image of λ is N^{d−2}HG^{2d−3}(X(C),Q/Z(d−1)).

items.name: Low-dimensional injectivity of Bloch's map
items.statement: For smooth proper X/R of dimension d≤3, Bloch's Abel–Jacobi map on torsion 1-cycles is injective.

items.name: Boundary preimage of coniveau under S54
items.statement: Under S54, the preimage of N^{d−2}HG^{2d−2}(X(C),Z(d−1)) by the coefficient boundary equals N^{d−2}HG^{2d−3}(X(C),Q/Z(d−1)).

items.name: Surjectivity of Bloch's map under real integral HC
items.statement: Under S54, λ:CH_1(X)_tors→HG^{2d−3}(X(C),Q/Z(d−1))_0 is surjective.

items.name: Abel–Jacobi isomorphism in dimension at most three
items.statement: Under S54 and d≤3, λ is an isomorphism CH_1(X)_tors≅HG^{2d−3}(X(C),Q/Z(d−1))_0.

items.name: Torsion 1-cycle orthogonality
items.statement: Under S54, cl_R(CH_1(X)[2∞]) and Im(HG²(X(C),Z(1))→HG²(X(R),Z(1))=H¹(X(R),F2)) are exact orthogonal complements.

items.name: Torsion cycles orthogonal to all divisor classes
items.statement: Under S54 with H²(O_X)=0, cl_R(CH_1(X)[2∞]) and cl_R(Pic(X)) are exact orthogonal complements.

items.name: Universal CH0 support for a smooth quartic threefold
items.statement: For a smooth quartic threefold X⊂P⁴_R and every algebraically closed extension C'/R, CH0(X_C') is supported on a point.
items.locator: Proposition5.7 proof; Roitman Theorem6 or rational connectedness of Fano varieties

items.name: Equivariant degree-four cohomology of a real-empty quartic
items.statement: For a smooth quartic threefold X⊂P⁴_R with X(R)=empty, HG⁴(X(C),Z(2))≅Z⊕F2, with the free summand generated by cl(L+conjugate L) for a complex line L⊂X_C.

items.name: Equivariant middle cohomology rank of a real-empty quartic
items.statement: For the same X, HG³(X(C),Z(2)) is finitely generated of rank thirty.

items.name: Torsion 1-cycles on a real-empty quartic
items.statement: If X⊂P⁴_R is a smooth quartic threefold with X(R)=empty and satisfies real integral HC for 1-cycles, then CH_1(X)_tors≅F2⊕(Q/Z)^30.

items.name: Part II input for quartics over ℝ
items.statement: A smooth quartic threefold over ℝ with no real points satisfies real integral HC for 1-cycles; this is imported from Part II §7, not proved in Part I.

items.name: Sketched full Chow group of a real-empty quartic
items.statement: For a smooth real-empty quartic threefold over ℝ, the source asserts CH_1(X)≅Z⊕F2⊕(ℝ/Z)^30.

items.name: Sketched real-point quartic torsion computation
items.statement: For the smooth real quartic x0⁴+x1⁴=x2⁴+x3⁴+x4⁴ in P⁴_ℝ, the source asserts CH_1(X)_tors≅F2⊕(Q/Z)^30.

items.name: Milnor K Gersten input for cohomology sheaves
items.statement: For smooth varieties in the characteristic-zero setting used here, the Gersten resolution for Milnor K-theory and its norm-residue comparison identify unramified torsion symbols with locally liftable integral cup products of unit classes.

items.name: Raising coniveau of the constant sign class
items.statement: For smooth projective X/R and n≥1, if ω^n∈H^n(X,Z_2(n)) has coniveau≥1 then ω^{n+1} has coniveau≥2; conversely this holds if CH0(X_C) is supported in dimension≤n−1.

items.name: Field level and vanishing of ω
items.statement: For a smooth integral variety X/R and n≥1, level(R(X))<2^n iff the mod-two class ω^n vanishes over R(X), equivalently the integral 2-adic ω^n has coniveau at least one on X.

items.name: Level bound for an anisotropic real quadric
items.statement: For the smooth anisotropic projective n-dimensional quadric over R, −1 is a sum of seven squares in its function field iff n≤6.

items.name: Witt–Pfister two-square theorem on real-empty curves
items.statement: For a smooth proper geometrically integral curve B over a real closed field with B(R)=empty, −1 is a sum of two squares in R(B). Consequently the nontrivial class of Br(R) becomes zero in Br(B).
items.locator: Lemma3.7 proof; Witt and Pfister inputs

items.name: Euler congruence in algebraic families
items.statement: For proper X/k and dimension-i cycles algebraically equivalent through a proper family, the Euler characteristics of their normalizations agree modulo ind_{i−1}(X).

items.name: Complex unramified 1-cycle defect
items.statement: For smooth connected projective complex d-fold X with CH0(X) supported on a surface, H^{d−3}(X,H_X^d(Q/Z(d−1)))≅Z^{2d−2}(X), the finite integral Hodge defect.

items.name: Definable sets and cell decomposition over a real closed field
items.statement: Use the existing LD.6 direction for semialgebraic definable sets, finite cell decompositions and definable maps over real closed fields; BW's sheaf, support and duality additions import that geometry rather than introduce a second definability library.

items.name: Ordinary cohomology and manifold duality import
items.statement: Import ordinary singular cohomology, cup products, orientation local coefficients, proper manifold pushforward and Poincaré duality from Algebraic Topology stage6, with its stage2 and5 prerequisites; construct only the semialgebraic/equivariant extensions and compatibility beyond it.

items.name: Cohomology theory with algebraic supports
items.statement: Let S_k be a full subcategory of algebraic k-schemes stable under étale extensions, containing Spec k and P¹_X for X∈S_k. A cohomology theory with supports is a contravariant graded abelian-group functor on pairs (X,Z closed), with natural localization LES for Z⊂Y⊂X; morphisms f satisfy f^−1(Z)⊆Z'.

api.name: RealCycles.supportTheory.characterise
api.statement: Localization compares h_Z(X),h_Y(X),h_{Y−Z}(X−Z) with a boundary.

api.name: RealCycles.supportTheory.compatibility
api.statement: A complex-valued substratum C(X) gives supported objects by the homotopy fiber C(X)→C(X−Z).

api.name: RealCycles.supportTheory.functoriality
api.statement: Étale excision COH1 means invariance under étale neighborhoods inducing an isomorphism on Z.

items.name: Strict effaceability
items.statement: For smooth affine X∈S_k and finitely many points t_i, a theory is strictly effaceable at them if for every neighborhood W, p≥0 and closed Z⊂W of codimension≥p+1, there are a neighborhood U⊂W of the t_i and closed Z'⊂W containing Z with codimension≥p such that h_Z∩U^q(U)→h_Z'∩U^q(U) is zero for every q.

api.name: RealCycles.strictEffaceable.characterise
api.statement: One common neighborhood and enlarged support work for all cohomological degrees.

api.name: RealCycles.strictEffaceable.compatibility
api.statement: The allowed support codimension drops by at most one.

api.name: RealCycles.strictEffaceable.functoriality
api.statement: For substrata replace the zero-on-cohomology condition by a nullhomotopy.

items.name: Homotopy invariance supplies the key lemma
items.statement: Under CHK Assumption5.1.6, support homotopy invariance COH3 implies the P¹ key-lemma identity COH2, which implies equality of the pullbacks along zero and infinity COH4. The analogous implications hold for substrata up to homotopy.

items.name: Bloch–Ogus–Gabber effacement criterion
items.statement: If k is infinite, S_k satisfies CHK Assumption5.1.6 and a cohomology theory with supports satisfies étale excision COH1 and the P¹ key lemma COH2, then it is strictly effaceable on smooth affine schemes at finite sets of points.

items.name: Flasque Cousin resolution criterion
items.statement: Under the effacement theorem's hypotheses, the Cousin complexes on each smooth X∈S_k are flasque resolutions of the Zariski cohomology sheaves H^q; therefore E2^{p,q}=H^p_Zar(X,H^q).

items.name: Explicit form of the derived integral cup product
items.statement: In the diagram of the proof of Proposition1.7, the map H^{i-d}(X(R), τ_{>0}(e)) is given by x ↦ xγ̃ + β_{ℤ̃}(x)β_{ℤ̃}(γ̃), where γ̃ ∈ H^0 ⊕ H^2 ⊕ ··· is the unique class with γ = γ̃ + β_{ℤ̃}(γ̃). In particular the derived cup product with integral coefficients, read through the canonical twisted integral decomposition (1.29), is not the sum of the individual cup product maps, in contrast with ℤ/2ℤ coefficients, where it is, by (1.28).
items.locator: Remark1.9, on the diagram in the proof of Proposition1.7

items.name: Euler-characteristic map does not factor through homological equivalence over general fields
items.statement: For X smooth and proper over an arbitrary field and i an integer, sending an integral dimension-i cycle to the Euler characteristic of its structure sheaf gives CH_i(X) → ℤ/elw_{i-1}(X)ℤ, which factors through algebraic equivalence (Kóllar, Proposition14). Over a real closed field and for i = 1 it factors even through homological equivalence, by Theorem3.6. This does not extend to arbitrary fields: let X be the smooth projective quadric threefold over ℂ((t))((u))((v)) defined by the anisotropic quadratic form ⟨1,t,u,tu,v⟩. Then H^4_ét(X,ℤ_2(2)) is torsion-free, while CH_1(X)_tors has order 2 and is generated by a class whose image in ℤ/elw_0(X)ℤ = ℤ/2ℤ does not vanish.

items.name: Sharpness of the vanishing hypothesis for the half-dimension bound
items.statement: There exist surfaces X over ℝ with H^2(X,O_X) ≠ 0, for instance K3 surfaces, for which H^1(X(ℝ),ℤ/2ℤ) ≠ 0 but H^1_alg(X(ℝ),ℤ/2ℤ) = 0. Hence the hypothesis H^2(X,O_X) = 0 cannot be dropped from Corollary3.20 and from its consequence that H^1(X(ℝ),ℤ/2ℤ) ≠ 0 implies H^1_alg(X(ℝ),ℤ/2ℤ) ≠ 0.

items.name: Quadratic eigenspaces for the displayed cyclic action
items.statement: For g=f² and w=(1,7,2,6,3,5,0), the weight-r quadratic space is spanned by x_i x_j with i≤j and w_i+w_j=r modulo8. Weights0,2,4,6 have dimension4, the other weights dimension3. The four defining spaces Λ_i have weight2i.

items.name: Conjugate pullback on the quadratic equation space
items.statement: For the displayed f, define T(Q)(x)=conjugate(Q(f(x))). This is an invertible conjugate-linear operator on complex quadrics, T²=g*, and T sends weight r to weight−r. If a reduced projective subvariety Y is f-stable then T preserves its degree-two vanishing ideal.

items.name: The weight-four space has no conjugate-pullback-stable line
items.statement: On the basis (a,b,c,d)=(x0x4,x1x5,x2²,x3²), T(Aa+Bb+Cc+Dd)=conjugate(B)a−conjugate(A)b+conjugate(D)c−conjugate(C)d. Consequently T²=−id and no nonzero one-dimensional complex subspace of Λ_2 is T-stable.
items.locator: Example4.4, published p.59; extracting-worker proof in report

items.name: Four defining quadrics generate the quadratic vanishing space
items.statement: Let Q0,...,Q3 be four complex quadrics defining a smooth scheme-theoretic complete intersection surface Y in P⁶. Then H⁰(P⁶,I_Y(2)) is their four-dimensional complex span. In particular, if Qi has distinct g*-weight2i, its intersection with Λ_2 is exactly C Q2.
items.locator: Example4.4, published p.59; extracting-worker proof in report

items.name: Exceptional restriction has the negative tautological sign
items.statement: In Lemma2.14 let ξ=c1(O_E(1)), δ=Σ_j ξ^(k−j)τ*β_j, and γ−π*α=Σ_j i_*(ξ^(k−j−1)τ*β_j). Then i*(γ−π*α)=−δ, because N_(E/Xtilde)=O_E(−1). Since the admissible classes form a subgroup, admissibility of the left side is equivalent to admissibility of δ.

items.name: Voisin's question on rationally connected varieties (statement only)
items.statement: Does every smooth proper rationally connected complex variety satisfy the integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles? Open; not asserted.
items.note: A question the paper raises; it is recorded as a statement, not as a result.

items.name: Algebraicity of ω^{2d−2} without real points (statement only)
items.statement: Is there a smooth proper variety X of odd dimension d over a real closed field R with X(R) = ∅ such that ω^{2d−2} is not algebraic? Open; not asserted.

items.name: Real integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles (statement only)
items.statement: For smooth proper geometrically irreducible X over R whose complexification is a uniruled threefold, a Calabi–Yau threefold or rationally connected, does X satisfy the real integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles? Open; not asserted (Part II answers some cases).

items.name: Cycle-theoretic obstruction under the complex IHC (statement only)
items.statement: Is there a smooth proper geometrically irreducible X over R such that X_C satisfies the complex integral Hodge conjecture for 1-cycles but X has a cycle-theoretic obstruction to the surjectivity of φ? Open over R; Part II gives non-archimedean examples.
